question.problem:
The matrix $A$ is given below. Let $\mathbf{a}_1$, $\mathbf{a}_2$,  $\mathbf{a}_3$, and $\mathbf{a}_4$ be the respective columns of $A.$ Determine if ![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/foundations/14128538/assets/afbd6ce90f2192c311c38ced9c1d9512c48bbf9a5e06236415ef9fe70883f9be.svg) is a basis of $\textrm{Col}(A).$ If that is the case, find $x_1 \cdot x_2$, where $\mathbf{a}_4=x_1\mathbf{a}_1+x_2\mathbf{a}_2.$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/foundations/14128538/assets/e2ccba053acf8d050e305c3768c970ae635f4583163a867b6ef11f4e565ac1ae.svg)
question.worked_solution:
First, we reduce the matrix $A$ to reduced row echelon form (RREF):

$$
\begin{aligned}A & =[\begin{aligned}2 & 0 & -4 & 4 \\ 0 & 1 & -6 & -3 \\ 1 & 2 & -14 & -4\end{aligned}] & {R}_{1} & :=\frac{1}{2}{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & -2 & 2 \\ 0 & 1 & -6 & -3 \\ 1 & 2 & -14 & -4\end{aligned}] & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}+(-1){R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & -2 & 2 \\ 0 & 1 & -6 & -3 \\ 0 & 2 & -12 & -6\end{aligned}] & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}+(-2){R}_{2} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & -2 & 2 \\ 0 & 1 & -6 & -3 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

From the matrix above, we see that the pivot columns are the $1$st and $2$nd columns. So, a basis of $\textrm{Col}(A)$ is $\{\mathbf{a}_1,\mathbf{a}_2 \},$ that is to say,
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/foundations/14128538/assets/6b4306172b78c1e59bf66c8c08bf864aac2bcab65d4b1cc08ba4ddab0e5f1da3.svg)

Now, since the $4$th column of the reduced matrix is a non-pivot column, then the entries in that column tell us the coefficients needed to express $\mathbf{a}_4$ as a linear combination of all the other columns in the original matrix. So, we have

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/foundations/14128538/assets/b3681d7f6c71d06ede32616ceec12ccd71da28373ee88eab451211af5a579212.svg)

This gives us $x_1 \cdot x_2 = 2 \cdot (-3) = -6.$
